entry.title: Meta launches Muse Wonder and Wonder Full for AI agents (2 minute read)
entry.content:
Muse Wonder is now available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code. Muse Wonder Full is available only to Muse Code subscribers. The new models combine Active Memory, which carries important personal context across conversations and retrieves relevant details when a task calls for them, with Active Focus, a feature designed to keep the model working through difficult goals by trying alternative approaches, handling blockers, adapting to new information, requesting clarification when needed, and checking before important actions. Meta says Muse Wonder is its most aligned model yet.

entry.title: Microsoft Prepares to Put Gigawatts of Its Chips in Data Centers (3 minute read)
entry.content:
Microsoft's newest iteration of its Maia chips will start rolling out next year. The Maia 300 is designed to handle inference. Microsoft expects to stock multiple gigawatts of the chips at its server farms. The Maia 300 delivers 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems. Microsoft isn't currently planning to rent the underlying computing power of Maia chips directly to its cloud customers.

entry.title: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. What's next for human employees? (23 minute read)
entry.content:
Amazon already has more than a million robots working in its warehouses, and it is poised to significantly grow that robotic fleet in the coming years. Amazon is also the second largest corporate employer in the world. The company's executives say the growing robot fleet has eased the burden on its human workforce, but labor advocacy groups and independent researchers say the warehouse automation is not all upside for the humans working alongside robots. It can get complicated when humans are expected to keep pace with their robotic counterparts.

entry.title: Is ‘Attention' the Essence of Intelligence? (14 minute read)
entry.content:
Research suggests that human thought is not purely linguistic. More brain regions light up than just the areas associated with language when we are thinking. Language may be how we communicate about the world, but our thoughts seem to draw on many other areas outside of the brain's language networks. AI's ability to translate effectively means that it can understand, in some sense.

entry.title: Why WebMCP matters (12 minute read)
entry.content:
Co-browsing needs to work really well for users for the web to succeed in the agentic age. It is the only model where the developer and the user maintain control over the experience, and where the web remains the web. WebMCP enables sites to provide agents with direct JavaScript tools they can call to accomplish tasks, which makes direct interaction significantly faster, better, and cheaper. It circumvents the slowness and awkwardness of AI agents trying to figure out how to interact with sites.

entry.title: Muse Wonder: Zuckerberg and Wang's $100B AI (130 minute read)

entry.title: Problems in 22 scientific fields had solutions hiding in plain sight. An AI has found them (7 minute read)
entry.content:
Borrowing an idea from one research discipline to solve a problem in another is an age-old scientific trick. However, such clever leaps are rare because researchers don't tend to spend their time researching fields outside of their expertise. AI can easily hop between fields. BootLoops is a harness that can spot and solve problems in seemingly unrelated fields that share the same mathematical structures at massive scale. Researchers recently released 36 preprints produced with BootLoops covering a wide range of topics, including figuring out the age of sunspots, analyzing government health policies, and attempting to decipher a mysterious medieval manuscript.

entry.content:

entry.title: In Vienna and Beijing, the First Nuclear Clocks Begin to Tick (6 minute read)
entry.content:
Two independent teams in Vienna and Beijing have simultaneously built the first clocks that keep time by counting the squishing and unsquishing of the atomic nuclei of thorium. The clocks are so precise that they only lose one second once every few million years or so. Nuclear clocks have the ability to search for certain kinds of dark matter. If a particle of dark matter passes through the thorium nuclei, it could register as a wobble in the nuclear clock's otherwise steady tick-tock.

Focus on sharpening your craft, turning ideas into stories people can retell, packaging your thinking so it travels without you, and helping your peers hit their goals.

entry.title: Anti-Patterns in Software Blogging (12 minute read)
entry.content:
Readers need a compelling reason quickly to continue reading. The reader should be able to read an article from start to finish without clicking links or hovering for tooltips. Avoid presenting articles as a follow-up to a previous article. Drop the formality and write the way you speak in real life. Test articles in mobile view, and use browser testing tools to find low-contrast text to improve visibility.
